patients.summary: Laboratory technician who joined in 2022 with chronic low back pain on as-needed oxycodone. Her third pregnancy (2024-2025) brought a suspicious right thyroid nodule, right otosclerosis, short cervix, placenta accreta, listeriosis and acute calculous cholecystitis, ending in cesarean hysterectomy at 35 weeks and an interval cholecystectomy. Postpartum thyroid FNA was benign with a repeat due September 2026.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is Susan Richard, 25, moving her care here from her old practice. Says she has chronic low back pain and takes oxycodone that her prior doctor wrote for; she wants to make sure there is no gap in that. Explained the membership and that the doctor will review the prior records before taking over any controlled prescription. New patient visit booked for 8/16 at 9:00. Records release form emailed to her, she will sign and send back today.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 25 y/o woman establishing care. Transferring from her prior practice, which she left because of the drive.

CC: chronic low back pain, wants continuity of her pain medicine.

HPI: Low back pain for several years, mechanical, no radiation into the legs, no numbness or weakness, no bowel or bladder change. Prior doctor has prescribed oxycodone 5 mg as needed; she takes 2-3 a day on work days, fewer on weekends. Works as a lab technician and is on her feet much of the shift, which is when it is worst. Never had imaging that she recalls. Denies taking more than prescribed, denies other substances. No other medicines.

PMH: chronic low back pain. Otherwise healthy.
OB: G2P2, two term vaginal deliveries, both uncomplicated.
PSH: none.
Meds: oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with hypothyroidism and a goiter. Father has had gallstones. Maternal grandmother had otosclerosis (hearing loss).
SH: married, two children at home. Lab technician. Never smoker, no alcohol, no drug use.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Well appearing, pleasant. HEENT normal. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Back: no midline tenderness, mild paraspinal tightness in the lumbar region, full forward flexion with some discomfort at end range. Straight leg raise negative both sides. Strength 5/5 lower extremities, reflexes 2+ and symmetric, sensation intact.

A/P:
1. Chronic low back pain, mechanical, no red flags. Will continue oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn, #90 per 30 days, prescribing from here going forward once her old records arrive. Controlled substance agreement reviewed and signed today. PDMP checked, consistent with her report, single prescriber.
2. Health maintenance: baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH (family history), HIV and hep C screening today. Pap per prior records, will confirm date. Flu and COVID in the fall.

Follow up 3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received 41 pages from the patient's previous primary care office. Summary for the chart:
- Problem list: chronic low back pain.
- Medications: oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed, monthly fills, signed opioid agreement on file there.
- Cervical cytology 2021: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Immunizations: childhood series complete, HPV series complete as a teen, Tdap with each prior pregnancy.
- Obstetric: two term vaginal deliveries.
Scanned to media. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Your labs from your first visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Susan, good to meet you this week. Your blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol and thyroid all came back in the normal range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Your old records came in too, so I'll be sending your oxycodone from here starting with your next fill. Text me if you need anything before November.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I have about 3 days of my oxycodone left. Can you send the next one to the same pharmacy? Thanks

documents.title: RE: Refill request
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent, 30 day supply. PDMP looks fine.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in after her shift for flu and bivalent COVID booster. Not pregnant, feeling well, no fever. Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Pfizer bivalent 0.3 mL IM left deltoid. VIS given for both. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction.

documents.title: Follow-up: chronic low back pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back about the same, 4/10 most days, worse at the end of long shifts. Using oxycodone 2/day on average, never more than 4. No leg symptoms. Sleeping okay. Kids keep her busy.
O: Vitals as charted. Lumbar paraspinals mildly tender, gait normal, SLR negative.
A/P: Chronic low back pain, stable on current regimen. PDMP reviewed. Continue oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn, #90/30 days. Encouraged walking and core work at home. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Prior authorization renewal - oxycodone
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy faxed that her plan wants a new prior auth for oxycodone 5 mg for the new year. Completed the insurer form with diagnosis and agreement date, submitted online. Approved same afternoon through 12/31. Pharmacy notified, patient texted that it's ready.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video visit: back pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit on her lunch break.
Winter has been a little harder on her back, 5/10, mostly stiffness in the morning. Still averaging two tablets a day. No new symptoms, no numbness, no weakness. Exam limited to video: moves comfortably, sits and stands without difficulty.
Assessment: chronic low back pain, no change. PDMP checked. Continue current dose. Heat in the mornings, stretching routine reviewed. See her in the office in the spring with her physical.

documents.title: New pharmacy
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My pharmacy in town is closing. Can you send my next oxycodone to the one on Route 9 instead? Due on Friday.

documents.title: RE: New pharmacy
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Updated your pharmacy in the chart. Doctor will send the new prescription Thursday so it is ready Friday.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26 y/o here for her yearly physical.

Interval: no illnesses. Back pain steady, using oxycodone about twice a day, agreement current. Works full time in the lab, kids are 'a handful but good.' Sleeping six to seven hours.

Meds: oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn. Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol. Wears seat belt. Exercises by walking a few times a week.
Screening: PHQ-9 2, GAD-7 3.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Eyes and ears normal, hearing grossly intact to conversation. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement or nodule. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Back unchanged from prior, neuro intact. Skin without concerning lesions.

Plan:
- Health maintenance: Pap up to date (2021, normal), due 2024. CBC and CMP today. Flu and COVID in the fall.
- Chronic low back pain: continue current plan, PDMP reviewed.
- Contraception: not using hormonal contraception, she and her husband use condoms; no plans for another pregnancy right now.
RTC 3 months for back pain.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Susan, your blood counts and chemistry panel from yesterday are all normal. Nothing to do. See you in August.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient did not arrive for 3:30 follow-up. Called and texted. She called back at 4:05, got stuck at work covering a coworker's shift. Rebooked 8/29.

documents.title: Back pain follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry about last week, short-staffed at work. Back has been better over the summer, 3/10, using 1-2 tabs most days. No new symptoms. Exam: normal gait, mild lumbar paraspinal tenderness, neuro intact. Chronic low back pain, improved. PDMP reviewed, fills on schedule. Continue oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn #90; she may not need all of them, okay to fill later if so. 3 months.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu (quadrivalent) 0.5 mL IM R deltoid and 2023-24 Pfizer COVID 0.3 mL IM L deltoid. Screening questions negative, not pregnant. VIS provided. Observed 15 min, tolerated well.

documents.title: Chronic pain follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective: Back 4/10 with the cold. Function good, working full time, no missed days. Averaging 2 tablets daily. No sedation, no constipation to speak of. Denies other substances.
Objective: Vitals as charted. Lumbar ROM full with end-range discomfort, SLR negative, strength and reflexes normal.
Assessment/plan: Chronic low back pain on stable low-dose opioid. Annual agreement renewed and signed, PDMP reviewed. Talked about whether she wants to try coming down on the dose; she prefers to keep things as they are for now and we will revisit. Continue oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn #90. Next visit in about 3 months.
